narrative.overview:
Learnova's visual system is built for the professional who has chosen to learn with intent. The surface is clean because the work is serious. Whitespace is not decorative emptiness; it is the margin on a well-used desk. Every element is present because it belongs, not because it fills space, or signals effort, or performs capability.

The interface does not congratulate you for opening it. It is already arranged, already ready. The Forest Focus Green of Salem anchors action with a color that earns attention without demanding it. Inter handles information with precision, never straining for personality it doesn't need. Shadows mark layer boundaries, not importance.

This system explicitly rejects: the bazaar-style urgency of Udemy; the cold institutional bureaucracy of Coursera; the dated clutter of Moodle; the badge-and-XP-explosion theater of generic LMS dashboards; and the overworked SaaS aesthetic of hero-metric grids and glassmorphism used as decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Forest Focus Green as the sole action anchor on neutral surfaces
Inter at every scale, differentiated by weight and size contrast only
Structural shadows on layer boundaries; flat within layers
Salem carries no more than 15% of any product screen's surface area
Generous whitespace as the primary rhythm mechanism, varied deliberately
No gradient text, no glassmorphism, no side-stripe accent borders

rules.name: The Forest Rule
rules.body: Salem is the single voice for action. One primary button per view section. If everything is Salem, nothing is.

rules.name: The Field Rule
rules.body: Coral and Anzac are earned, not applied. Coral appears when something requires the user's attention. Anzac appears when the user has completed something. Neither is available for decoration.

rules.name: The On-Dark Rule
rules.body: On Salem full-bleed sections, body copy uses white at 85% opacity; headings use white at 100%. Neutral Field colors are never used on Salem backgrounds.

rules.name: The Single Typeface Rule
rules.body: Inter handles every scale. No second typeface for personality. The script wordmark lives in the logo SVG only.

rules.name: The Scale Ratio Rule
rules.body: Each step in the hierarchy is at least 1.25x larger than the one below it. Never introduce an in-between size as a third level in the same zone.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Cards, panels, and form elements carry no shadow at rest. Shadow appears only when an element changes stacking context (dropdown, modal) or responds to hover (interactive cards only).

dos: Do use Salem (#0B6E4F) as the sole filled-button color. Its authority comes from scarcity: no more than 15% of any product screen's surface.
Do use whitespace as the primary rhythm mechanism. Vary padding between sections deliberately.
Do use tonal layering (bg-base, surface, surface-elevated) to communicate depth before reaching for a shadow.
Do use Anzac and Coral in status-bearing contexts only: completion moments, warnings, streaks.
Do apply structural shadows only to surfaces that change stacking context.
Do handle prefers-reduced-motion on all entrance animations.
Do present one primary button per view zone.
Do write button and nav labels in sentence case.
donts: Don't replicate Udemy's urgency patterns: no Best Seller badges, no countdown timers, no discount language on thumbnails.
Don't use Coursera's corporate-blue-and-white palette. Scholar Blue is a secondary data-context color only.
Don't adopt Moodle-style dense enterprise layouts.
Don't add XP explosions, leaderboards, or trophy dashboards.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient fill).
Don't use glassmorphism decoratively. Backdrop blur exists only on the sticky navbar in its scrolled state.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe.
Don't build identical-card grids. Same-sized icon-heading-text cards in a repeating grid is the default AI reflex for this category.
Don't add shadow to elements at rest if they do not change stacking context.
Don't use the hero-metric template: big number, small label, supporting stat, gradient accent.
Don't write em dashes in UI copy. Use commas, colons, or periods instead.
Don't use Salem as an ambient background on product surfaces.
